Summary: Gnosticism was a diverse movement in the 1st and 2nd centuries that taught salvation comes through secret knowledge. It often viewed the material world as evil and created by a lesser god.
Beliefs: Salvation comes through secret knowledge; The material world is evil; The God of the Old Testament is a lesser creator; Jesus brought hidden knowledge for the spiritual elite
Controversy: Opposed by early church writers such as Irenaeus in Against Heresies (c. AD 180) and by the formation of the New Testament canon
ChristianResponse: The church affirmed that creation is good, salvation is by grace through faith in Christ, and the gospel is openly proclaimed, citing Genesis 1 and John 1.
